comments.body: Two more instances, 2026-11-07, Muster 0.23.0, Mac, Fencil parallel-work round: worker easel ran report --waiting "second review round from tabby" and worker lagoon ran report --waiting "Codex reviewer knot on 35e4d5b", both without --until-message-from (checked in their transcripts). Each got its review, reported done and went idle; muster window still showed easel waiting 3 minutes later, and @muster told the integrator 10 minutes later that lagoon had been waiting on knot. Where they took the plain form from is not known; the session-start hook text shows it.

comments.body: 2026-11-09 re-triage, two more instances where the command was not recorded, both ending in a false 10-minute notice to an integrator: Lectern round (Mac mini, 2026-11-09): worker umber declared 'waiting on Codex review of the margin (yucca)', got the review, posted 'slot 2 done' and went idle; yucca's pane was gone and the wait still showed. agent-engine round 1 (2026-11-09): worker pelican declared a wait on Codex reviewer sandal's re-review, reported done, was compacted and began a new brief; @muster then told integrator peach pelican had been waiting on sandal for 10 minutes. Moved to backlog-hi: integrators lose time to these notices in nearly every round. A case where the flag was given and the wait still outlived the reply is a_2x1XwUfGo. From tooling feedback a_2sIzxTThc.

comments.body: 2026-11-09 re-triage: moved to the top of next. It is a small docs change in the two adapters' session-start hooks, and its symptom costs integrators a false notice in most parallel-work rounds.

comments.body: Done in 600af81b: the Claude Code and Codex session-start hooks add 'When it is an answer from another pane, add --until-message-from <its callsign>: without it the wait outlives the answer.' OpenCode's plugin carries no such line.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-11-05 on 0.22.0 on the devenv, five times in one parallel-work round. A Claude Code worker declared a wait on its reviewer helper before ending its turn, for example `"$MUSTER_DAEMON" report --waiting "on ferret re-check"`, got the review, posted its done report, took a new brief, planned through several turns and was compacted with `muster pane compact`. Through all of it `muster window` showed it `waiting ... on ferret re-check`, so `muster pane wait --until idle` timed out on an agent sitting idle at its prompt. In the other four, 10 minutes after the wait was declared, @muster told the integrator the worker 'had been waiting on <reviewer>'s re-check for 10 minutes. Check whether it still needs help', though it had reported done and gone idle.

This is the documented behavior for a wait declared without `--until-message-from`: a message wake carries it, for up to 10 minutes per carry. a_2q5wUnqa4 added the flag for exactly this case, and docs/cli/agents.md and the muster skill show it. The session-start hook in extras/claude-code/hooks/hooks.json (and extras/codex) does not: it says only 'Only when you end a turn to wait on work you started (a build, a background job, a sub-agent), first run "$MUSTER_DAEMON" report --waiting "<what>"'. An agent that knows Muster from the hook alone declares the wait without the flag. The first instance's command shows no flag; the other four commands were not recorded.

Costs: one false 'still needs help' notice per worker per round for the integrator, each a wake and a pane read to rule out, and `pane wait --until idle` timeouts.

Possibly: have the hook text name the flag for a wait on another agent (`--until-message-from <pane>`), or drop 'a sub-agent' from what the hook says to declare.
title: The session-start hook teaches report --waiting without --until-message-from, so a wait on a reviewer outlives the review
